QUIBBLE.name: Bill
QUIBBLE.direction: Old pompous pirate captain, gravelly theatrical boasts.

FINE PRINT.name: Charlie
FINE PRINT.direction: Quick, mischievous parrot, bright emphatic comic delivery.

NELL.name: Alice
NELL.direction: Clear, lively young adventurer; curious and dryly amused.

MARA.name: Matilda
MARA.direction: Warm, grounded tavern keeper; measured delivery and dry humour.

ORIN.name: Bill
ORIN.direction: Low, seasoned older navigator; unhurried storyteller.

records.text: Why check again?
A chart tells you where somebody measured. The current water tells you whether to sail.
Who owns Second Opinion?
I do. Cooperation has not altered the registration.
Can we turn back?
Finish the handover or restore central hold. Then we check the approach together.
The blank patch?
Beyond the marked reach I do not know the bottom. I have finally put that on paper.
My own boat?
Useful work, sound planks, clear terms. Destiny is a poor caulking material.
What does the bypass bypass?
Central command transmission. Not power, not public signals, and certainly not the need to think.
Who permits inspection?
The posted dry-maintenance provision. Named inspector, caretaker, current cover and seated holds. Not permission to do anything else.
Why this order?
Inlet relief first, outer return second, quay balance last. Balance needs both paths confirmed.
Can I undo it?
Hold positions. Disengage quay, outer, then inlet if active. Verify all pilots off before reconnecting central command.
Your name on the plate?
A name is useful when somebody needs the next inspection. A wage is useful when the inspector needs supper.
Exhibit Zero?
An empty display for something with a more impressive story than specification.
Do you deny the trial?
No. I defend a common schedule. You dispute the account condition. Let us not pretend those are the same question.
What about my calibration?
Your work was accurate. That fact will survive your disagreement with me.
Why not shared schedules?
Because I have watched everyone assume somebody else was responsible. You will have to show me names.
What counts as an emergency?
A stated hazard, publicly signalled. I expect you to take it seriously even when you dislike the speaker.
What work remains?
The return gauge still needs reading. Your victory has not made the metal self-maintaining.
Do you forgive us?
You have not asked for the kind of approval I can give. I suspect that is deliberate.
Revision two?
The quay is middle now. B balance. I will not turn an old answer into a new promise.
Are you ready to hold?
Yes. And I can say hold when you would rather hear go.
The old relief run?
My account remains mine. Do not improve the present case by moving somebody else into the past.
What changes now?
The next person gets the instructions and the right to question them.
Provisions?
Bread, tea, and a jar that has survived worse plans than yours.
Why B at the quay?
Its middle-level route is B. My outer station uses C at middle. Read the card for the machine in front of you.
Does local mean simple?
No. It means the people responsible can see and answer for the work.
Family credit?
Put the mistakes beside the drawings. Otherwise the next generation has to discover them again.
The sounding kit?
It measures depth, not worthiness. I have removed three unnecessary ambitions from the handle.
Why do you go first?
Relief must precede return and balance. My splendid rank has been omitted from the diagram.
Can you wait?
With distinction. Observe the flourish I am not making.
The bridge?
Open. A declaration that describes something is a surprisingly restful occupation.
One last duel?
Your argument has no legs!
And my reply?
Then we shall give it a sound footing. A draw. Public passage remains open.
Witness or judge?
Witness. A transcript is not a verdict, even when beautifully punctuated.
Why repeat Vane’s claim?
Because leaving it out would make our account less true.
Who pays for work?
People may pay for surveying and itemised maintenance without buying permission to exist on the water.
Represent me?
Subject to an agreement in which you are permitted to explain your own interests.
Boat name?
Still Deciding. A formidable obstacle to invoicing.
Another headline?
After the sources. Large type does not make a missing observation appear.
Print Vane’s answer?
Beside the records, with the date. Readers can do some of the work.
What did review decide?
Exclusive dispatch withdrawn. Maintenance obligations retained. History not rewritten.
Free chart, unpaid chartmaker?
Public reproduction and paid work are different terms. We can put both in the agreement.
Corrections?
A dated edition, a contact address, and somebody willing to be wrong in print.
Second Opinion is ready. I have not mistaken that for a weather report.
The stations are prepared. I have not mistaken that for today's permission.
Excellent. We are becoming extremely difficult to flatter into an accident.
Check the approach with me. Then we go.
You have made a very eloquent collection of dependencies.
Yes. I finally wrote down their names.
The dry changeover procedure is available. No part of that sentence says it is complete.
Emergency central authority. Local cover is unverified. Restore the central return.
Public declaration received. Claim recorded exactly.
Inlet relief is engaged and confirmed. I shall not improve that fact by shouting.
Keep the warning open. Check what it says.
If everyone can copy it, what are we paying you for?
Making it worth copying. And coming back when the water proves me wrong.
Good. I can print those terms without making them smaller.
Service Inlet. Relief open. Quibble, present and answering.
Outer Landing. Return established. Tamsin Rook. The numbers are agreeing without a family motto.
Repair Quay. Balance confirmed. Mara. I am staying until someone properly relieves me.
Three stations. Three names. One recorded watch.
Now check the boat. Being right about the gates is not the whole job.
Lighter clear of the western transit. No account presented. No scrape heard.
One passage does not maintain a harbour.
No. Neither does one director.
Your return gauge. What does it show?
Within the marked range.
Please put your name beside it.
Exclusive dispatch withdrawn. Maintenance obligations retained.
You have removed the convenient part.
The convenient part for whom?
That question is going above the fold.
Put the finding above it. People should be able to check the joke.
At last. A place for the accumulated substance of my adventures.
Is that a specimen?
Pocket lint. Provenance: pocket. Further provenance: uncertain.
I can catalogue that.
You can catalogue uncertainty?
Certainly. The trouble starts when people catalogue it as a crown.
Any special powers?
It has kept you from throwing away an empty pocket for five chapters.
Remarkable conservation work.
Bread. Tea. Something in a jar that will remain useful longer than either of us expects.
Advice?
Ask before you decide what someone else needs protecting from.
You could come for the first stretch.
Ask me tomorrow. I would like to answer without a crisis helping.
Here. Beyond this point I don't know the bottom.
You've left it blank.
A considerable improvement on what I used to do.
A sounding reel. It measures depth, not worthiness.
A narrow field for one of your family inventions.
I have removed three unnecessary ambitions from the handle.
I declare this crossing open.
It was open.
Yes. I am practising declarations that describe something.
A hundred copies. One correction address. No miraculous guarantees.
Put my name on it.
As owner of the water?
As the person to tell when the chart is wrong.
Your maintenance list has an unreasonable number of listeners.
Those are the people affected by the work.
I had inferred that.
Good. Read the first name back.
I could represent your interests.
Provided I get to tell you what they are.
An unusually demanding client. What will you call the boat?
Still Deciding.
Terrible name. Impossible to invoice.
You will find a way.
The dry route is open. The wet stair is still wet. I have resisted improving its description.
We check the current cover before we touch the bypass.
Good. I have put the instructions where the dramatic machinery cannot hide them.
Watch D, revision two. Outer high. Quay middle. Inlet low.
The quay has risen. Mara’s old A setting is no longer the answer.
The other settings still need new named replies. A familiar number is not a fresh observation.
You may inspect. You may even object. Neither activity gives you a harbour.
I brought a procedure, not a flag.
The dry changeover provision is posted. Its interlocks remain in force.
Command coupling open. Gate drive power retained. Public signals retained.
The centre can speak. It cannot move a local pilot through that gap.
Outer Landing. Tamsin Rook. Watch D, revision two. High, B return. Disengaged test passed; named readback confirmed.
Repair Quay. Mara. Watch D, revision two. Middle, B balance. The old A setting has been replaced and tested. I hold until the paths are confirmed.
Service Inlet. Quibble. Watch D, revision two. Low, C relief. Test passed. I shall be first because of the pipe, not my seniority.
A repaired hull, an itemised fitting bill, and work people actually need. That is a boat agreement, not a coronation.
And Second Opinion?
Still mine. I have had enough trouble finding her once.
Positions held. Disengage the active local pilots in reverse order. Reconnect only after every pilot answers disengaged.
Keep the evidence. We are reversing the controls, not what happened.
Full sequence. Declaration, readbacks, independent passage observation. The original stays in the recorder.
The shore transcript agrees. Including the sentences nobody wanted to hear again.
A named partner is not pocket-sized.
The original stays with its owner. Read it or request a witnessed copy.
Use the labelled room action to inspect this equipment safely.
A named partner, not an inventory item.
PILOT V5-1 / CURRENT VOYAGE. WEST SERVICE APPROACH. SLACK TURN. East company arm restricted. Do not use the earlier EBB board.
Fixed transit: WAREHOUSE CORNER / LIGHTHOUSE NOTCH aligned. Marked west service approach clear. Confirm again with Orin before each voyage.
Second Opinion: class S. Current marked west service route permits inspected class S vessels. Orin remains captain and owner.

DRY MAINTENANCE PROVISION: Named inspector and caretaker may perform a witnessed changeover with current local cover and seated gate-position holds. Isolate CENTRAL COMMAND TRANSMISSION only. Retain DRIVE POWER and PUBLIC SIGNAL. Inlet C relief → Outer B return → Quay B balance. Never reconnect central while a local pilot is engaged. This procedure does not adjudicate the charter.

DRY MAINTENANCE PROVISION: Named inspector and caretaker may perform a witnessed changeover with current local cover and seated gate-position holds. Isolate CENTRAL COMMAND TRANSMISSION only. Retain DRIVE POWER and PUBLIC SIGNAL. Inlet C relief → Outer B return → Quay B balance. Never reconnect central while a local pilot is engaged. This procedure does not adjudicate the charter.
DRY PERSONNEL ROUTE. Inspection telltale clear. Wet culvert inaccessible. Keep behind the glass and guard rails.
Outer, Quay, Inlet: mechanical position holds seated. Gates retain their held positions during the bounded command changeover.
COMMAND transmits central orders. DRIVE POWER powers both central and local equipment. PUBLIC SIGNAL carries warnings and named readbacks. Open command only; keep the other two continuous.
EMERGENCY RETURN is a public request, not an unconditional actuator. Reconnection requires all local pilots disengaged under witnessed hold. Emergency assistance remains available.
R17: trial command and acknowledgement. R18: calibration source Nell. R19: exclusive dispatch authorised, EXECUTION PENDING. The historical relief incident had a different operator.
Double circle: DIRECTOR ASSERTS EMERGENCY CENTRAL AUTHORITY. Claim: LOCAL COVER UNVERIFIED. Record and repeat publicly. A declaration alone is not independent hazard evidence.
Current named inlet physical return confirmed. Outer and Quay position holds seated. Watch D / revision 2. These reports describe present paused-stage cover, not future readiness.
Orin’s independent sighting: marked approach clear. No vessel in the changeover zone. Observation current for the paused check, not a permanent guarantee.
PUBLIC SUPPLY LIGHTER: class S; inspection passed; west service route clearance current; exclusive account NONE. Authorise one monitored passage only.
EXHIBIT ZERO — CLAIMS AWAITING EVIDENCE. CLEAN DISPLAY TRAY. NO MACHINE CONNECTION. An empty display for something with a more impressive story than specification.

HC-5 — Harbour charter review. Dispatch records establish an exclusive-account condition on ordinary passage, contrary to the public-service undertaking. An emergency assertion does not remove the duty to state and verify a hazard. Itemised maintenance charges and evidenced safety restrictions remain permissible. Exclusive dispatch privileges withdrawn. Fair Passage must provide records and supervised remedial work. The historic relief incident is not attributed to Director Vane. Review and correction records remain public.

PUBLIC WORKING EDITION 1. Fixed warehouse/lighthouse transit; dated soundings and vessel limits; distinct test, announcement, emergency and handover signals; station contacts and relief records; trained maintenance boundaries; unsurveyed reach explicitly blank. Corrections: Quay Quill and named station desks. Reproduction permitted. Surveying and itemised maintenance remain paid work.

Still Deciding: existing repair-yard hull and itemised fitting work as payment for completed surveys and defined future visits. Nell owns the vessel, may refuse unsafe work and grants public reproduction of agreed survey editions. No exclusive navigation rights, indefinite debt or transfer of Second Opinion. Weeks later: trained relief crews have signed the published station roster.
The water, not the account, decided who waited.
Every fee was illegal.
Two inspected boats met the same conditions; your slips name the missing contract.
R19 has already executed.
Your own work made the system accurate.
I never supplied calibration.
You caused the historic grounding.
I supplied calibration, not consent to exclusive dispatch.
Without central command you have three strangers pulling levers.
Three named attendants, one current revision, a tested sequence and a right to hold.
The Watch C model worked.
I will pull every lever myself.
Safety is a service. Service has a price.
All maintenance must be free.
Itemised maintenance may be charged; an exclusive account cannot condition ordinary passage.
All restrictions are unlawful.
Choose. My authority, or nobody responsible.
Give me sole control.
Smash the drum.
Shared responsibility is still responsibility. Record your instruction beside our answers.
Quiet dry harbour maintenance chamber, gentle distant water behind stone walls, faint brass machinery and warm wind, no voices no music, seamless loop.
Short mechanical brass test handle click and gentle indicator ratchet, no voices.
Two clear small brass harbour bells and a soft telephone relay click, no voices.
Old hand printing press rolling a sheet of paper, wood and metal creak, no voices.
